title: Proxy with basic authentication not working since Firefox 114+
body: I am using Firefox 117 on Linux. Starting with Firefox 114, HTTPS proxy servers requiring Basic authentication no longer work for me. I have tried FoxyProxy, SwitchyOmega, SmartProxy, and a PAC file. Requests to any website time out with NS_ERROR_NET_TIMEOUT instead of using the credentials saved in the add-on or asking for a username and password. The same proxy works in Chrome after its authentication prompt, and an unauthenticated proxy works in Firefox. This worked in Firefox 113. My additional testing suggests the HTTPS proxy protocol may be the distinguishing factor, rather than Basic authentication alone.

symptoms_visible: When I enable an HTTPS proxy requiring Basic authentication in Firefox 114 or later, every website eventually fails with NS_ERROR_NET_TIMEOUT.
Firefox neither uses the credentials stored by the proxy add-on nor displays an authentication prompt; the same proxy prompts and works in Chrome.
An unauthenticated proxy still works in Firefox, and the authenticated HTTPS proxy worked in Firefox 113.
N0.label: N0 authenticated HTTPS proxy timeout reported

symptoms_visible: The authenticated HTTPS proxy still times out in the bad builds selected by mozregression.
N1.label: N1 regression output collected

symptoms_visible: In a clean Firefox profile, opening a site through the authenticated HTTPS proxy still waits for about 30 seconds and then times out.
N2.label: N2 requested network and TLS log collected

symptoms_visible: The HTTPS proxy connection still times out even though this setup is intended to use only a proxy username and password.
N3.label: N3 expected authentication configuration clarified

symptoms_visible: With the same proxy, Firefox times out whether the add-on password is filled in or empty, while Chrome displays a Basic authentication prompt and then works.
N4.label: N4 comparative packet captures collected

symptoms_visible: I have not reported a retest on a build containing the landed change; the last behavior I personally reported was that Firefox timed out while Chrome worked.
N_terminal.label: terminal patch landed without reporter verification

question_patterns: Could you run mozregression and share the final bisection output?
Can you find the regression range between Firefox 113 and the first bad release?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran mozregression. Its final output prints: 'Bug 1289186 - wait for the server certificate to verify successfully before asking for a client auth certificate', followed by 'The bisection is done.'

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My run says the proxy already times out in the Firefox 113 builds, so it does not identify a change between 113 and 114.
I obtained the same final commit message after starting the bisection from a slightly different pair of good and bad builds.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c2-c3: participant1 requested mozregression and the reporter pasted its raw final commit message. The reporter also volunteered that the company proxy certificate is signed by an internal CA already imported into the system/browser trust store.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the timeout while recording about:logging with the requested networking, socket, TLS, and certificate-verifier modules?
Please collect a network and TLS log during one timed-out request and send it privately.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created a clean Firefox profile, configured FoxyProxy with the authenticated HTTPS proxy, enabled the requested logging modules, opened a website, and waited about 30 seconds for the timeout. I e-mailed the new log; it contains pipnss and certverifier messages.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the requested modules enabled, the clean profile loads the site successfully and I cannot reproduce the timeout.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c5-c8: the first log used default settings, so the reporter repeated the measurement with the requested modules and e-mailed the corrected private log. The clean-profile setup was volunteered with the answer.

question_patterns: Does this setup require the browser to present a certificate, or should it authenticate only with the proxy username and password?
Is a certificate from the client part of the expected proxy configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The connection should not use a client authentication certificate. There is only Basic authentication for the proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, our proxy requires both the username and password and a specific client certificate that is not installed in this Firefox profile.

edges.comment: Reporter configuration, c10-c12: participant2 initially noted that no usable client certificate was found. The reporter clarified that none should be required. Participant1 then read the private log as showing that proxy Basic authentication had already succeeded.

question_patterns: Can you capture the failing request in Firefox and a successful request through the same proxy in Chrome?
Please provide comparative packet captures for Firefox and Chrome using the same proxy.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made and e-mailed two captures: Firefox using the proxy and timing out, and Chrome using the same proxy successfully. Chrome displayed its Basic authentication window as soon as I enabled the proxy, before I started that capture. Firefox never displays the prompt, whether the FoxyProxy password is filled in or empty.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both Firefox and Chrome time out through the proxy in my captures, and neither browser reaches a successful connection.
The Firefox and Chrome outcomes are the same, but I started both captures before enabling the proxy, so the Chrome authentication exchange is included.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c13-c14: the reporter supplied private comparative captures and volunteered that before Firefox 114 the add-on credentials were used without showing a prompt. No packet-level causal conclusion was supplied by the reporter.

solution.intent: Fix the stalled tunneled TLS connection by notifying Necko when the asynchronous certificate-selection step completes and driving the TLS handshake again, rather than changing proxy Basic-auth credentials or requiring the user to install a client certificate.
solution.concrete_example: The log's HTTP/1.0 200 Connection Established means proxy Basic authentication succeeded. The timeout occurs afterward: certificate selection is deferred until server-certificate verification, but the lower TLS transport is not polled again because the poll flag is zero. Notify Necko when the selection completes and drive the handshake. The patch has landed; please retest in today's build and tell us whether sites load through the proxy.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw mozregression output, private logs, configuration facts, and packet captures. Engineers determined from those materials and a local reproduction that the proxy CONNECT had returned 200, the timeout occurred in the secondary TLS handshake, and a zero poll flag prevented the lower transport from being polled after asynchronous certificate selection. Those causal conclusions must not be placed in the user's answers.

edges.comment: Opening chain resolution, c12 and c15-c22: participant1 and participant2 interpreted the reporter's log, reproduced the tunneled TLS timeout locally, traced the stalled polling/handshake path, and landed a patch that lets Necko drive the handshake after certificate selection. Later ESR uplift and test-manifest coordination are omitted as release logistics. The original reporter never confirmed the landed fix on their own system, so this terminal snapshot remains unverified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: proxy Basic authentication succeeds, but the tunneled TLS handshake stalls after server-certificate verification and asynchronous certificate selection because the lower transport is not polled or driven again.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected regression output, corrected network/TLS log, expected no-client-certificate configuration, and comparative browser evidence rather than inferred from the timeout alone.
The technical fix must notify Necko when certificate selection completes and resume or drive the TLS handshake and transport polling.

Must not prescribe installing a client-authentication certificate or merely changing the proxy username/password as the fix; the reporter's configuration requires only Basic authentication and the log shows that stage succeeded.
Must ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing the fix and must not declare the issue user-verified at this thread snapshot, because no reporter retest was posted after the patch landed.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable enterprise Linux user. Familiar with proxy add-ons, PAC files, internal CA trust, clean-profile testing, and packet captures, but new to mozregression and dependent on engineers for low-level TLS and Necko interpretation.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and methodical. Provides detailed reproduction steps, corrects mistakes promptly, sends sensitive logs privately, and distinguishes observed behavior from uncertainty about the cause.
